question: Find the simple interest (in closest integral ₹) on ₹3,000 at 6% per annum rate of interest for the period from 9 February 2024 to 10 April 2024.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify **Leap Year**: 2024 is a leap year (366 days).

Total days = 20 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 10 (Apr) = 61 days.

Interest Calculation: Interest = (3000 × 6 × 61/366) / 100

Since 6 × 61 = 366, Interest = 3000 / 100 = 30.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹3,000

Rate (R) = 6% per annum

Time period = 9 February 2024 to 10 April 2024

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b1bb837c4f84eda72b744c2daca849df1504d6b5d06dfa7a34d1d256e88443a2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of days in **February** = 29 − 9 = 20 days (2024 is a **leap year**)

⇒ Number of days in **March** = 31 days

⇒ Number of days in **April** = 10 days

⇒ Total Days = 20 + 31 + 10 = 61 days

⇒ Time (T) in years = 61 / 366 years

⇒ SI = (3000 × 6 × (61/366)) / 100

⇒ SI = (3000 × 6 × 61) / (100 × 366)

⇒ SI = (3000 × 366) / (100 × 366)

⇒ SI = 3000 / 100

⇒ SI = ₹30

**∴ The correct answer is ₹30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Leap Year Calculation

A year is a **leap year** if it is divisible by 4. If it is a century year (ending in 00), it must be divisible by 400. Leap years have **366 days**.

Day Counting Rule

In banking and financial interest calculations, normally the **day of deposit** is excluded and the **day of withdrawal** is included (or vice versa).

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple interest is calculated only on the **principal**, while compound interest is calculated on the **principal plus accumulated interest** from previous periods.
